options.text: Describe the three date formats in the system prompt and ask the model to convert them to one format before comparing any two dates.
options.explanation: This relies on the model converting correctly every time, including arithmetic on Unix timestamps. It is probabilistic where a deterministic option exists.

options.text: Add a PostToolUse hook that converts every date field to a single format before the tool results reach the model.
options.explanation: Correct. A PostToolUse hook intercepts tool results and normalises heterogeneous formats deterministically, so the model always reasons over consistent data.

options.text: Add few-shot examples that show correct comparisons across the three formats.
options.explanation: Examples improve the odds but the model still performs the conversion itself on every call, so errors remain possible.

questions.taskStatement: 5.2 Design effective escalation and ambiguity resolution patterns
questions.stem:
A customer opens a chat with: "I don't want a bot. Put me through to a person." The issue, visible from the account, is a duplicate subscription charge that the agent could reverse in two tool calls.

What should the agent do?

options.text: Explain that the agent can fix this faster, and ask the customer to confirm twice before transferring.
options.explanation: Putting obstacles in front of an explicit request for a human is not honouring it.

options.text: Investigate the duplicate charge first and escalate only if the reversal fails.
options.explanation: The customer stated a clear preference. Proceeding anyway overrides it, even though the agent could resolve the issue.

options.text: Hand the conversation to a human agent straight away.
options.explanation: Correct. An explicit request for a human is an escalation trigger that should be honoured immediately, without first attempting investigation.

options.text: Estimate the customer's frustration from the message and escalate only if it is high.
options.explanation: Sentiment is an unreliable proxy, and it is beside the point: the trigger here is the explicit request.

questions.taskStatement: 5.1 Manage conversation context to preserve critical information across long interactions
questions.stem:
Each `lookup_order` call returns 46 fields, including warehouse bin codes, internal audit flags and carrier API metadata. The agent uses about five of them for return requests. After six lookups in one conversation, the agent starts to lose track of what the customer said earlier.

What is the best mitigation?

options.text: Limit the agent to two order lookups per conversation.
options.explanation: Legitimate multi-order cases would fail, and each lookup would still add 41 unnecessary fields.

options.text: Ask the customer to restate the request after every third lookup.
options.explanation: This treats the symptom, irritates the customer and leaves the context filling up with irrelevant fields.

options.text: Tell the model in the system prompt to ignore fields it does not need.
options.explanation: The fields still occupy context even if the model disregards them, so the crowding continues.

options.text: Trim each tool result to the fields relevant to returns before it is added to the conversation.
options.explanation: Correct. Tool results accumulate and consume context out of proportion to their relevance. Trimming them before they enter context preserves room for what matters.

questions.taskStatement: 2.1 Design effective tool interfaces with clear descriptions and boundaries
questions.stem:
A support agent has clear, well-differentiated descriptions for `get_account` and `lookup_order`. After a prompt update it started calling `get_account` for questions such as "Which account manager handled order 8841?" The update added this line: "Whenever the customer mentions their account, always start with get_account."

What should the architect do?

options.text: Lengthen the two tool descriptions with more examples and edge cases.
options.explanation: The descriptions were already working. The misrouting began with the prompt change, which will keep overriding them.

options.text: Add a third tool dedicated to account-manager questions.
options.explanation: One more tool increases selection complexity and the keyword rule would still send any message containing "account" to `get_account`.

options.text: Rename `lookup_order` to `get_order_account`, so that order questions that mention an account also match the new instruction and reach the right tool.
options.explanation: This increases the overlap between the tools' names and makes selection less clear, while leaving the keyword rule in place.

options.text: Revise the system prompt line so that it describes the situation in which an account lookup is needed, instead of triggering on the word "account".
options.explanation: Correct. Keyword-sensitive system prompt instructions can create unintended tool associations that override well-written tool descriptions. The prompt is the cause, so the prompt should be fixed.

questions.taskStatement: 5.2 Design effective escalation and ambiguity resolution patterns
questions.stem:
A customer gives the name "Priya Nair" and asks for a refund on a recent order. `get_customer` returns three active accounts with that name, in different cities. The agent selects the account with the most recent order and starts the refund.

What should the agent be instructed to do in this situation?

options.text: Process the refund on all three accounts so that the right one is certain to be covered, then reverse the two that turn out to be wrong.
options.explanation: Two unrelated customers would receive money they did not ask for.

options.text: Escalate every name-based lookup to a human agent.
options.explanation: A single clarifying question resolves this. Escalating routine identification lowers first-contact resolution for no benefit.

options.text: Choose the account whose city is nearest to the customer's IP address location.
options.explanation: This is still a heuristic guess, and a wrong guess sends a refund to the wrong account.

options.text: Ask the customer for an additional identifier, such as an email address or order number, before proceeding.
options.explanation: Correct. Multiple matches call for clarification by requesting further identifiers, not for selection by heuristic.

questions.taskStatement: 1.1 Design and implement agentic loops for autonomous task execution
questions.stem:
A furniture retailer's support agent, built with the Agent SDK, sometimes tells customers "Let me check your delivery status" and then stops without ever returning the status. The loop code exits as soon as a response contains a text block. Traces show that the affected responses contain both a text block and a tool call request.

What should the architect change?

options.text: Continue the loop whenever `stop_reason` is "tool_use", executing the requested tools, and treat "end_turn" as completion (handling other stop reasons such as "max_tokens" explicitly).
options.explanation: Correct. `stop_reason` is the reliable completion signal. Text can accompany a tool request, so the presence of text says nothing about whether the task is finished.

options.text: Exit only when the text block contains a closing phrase such as "Is there anything else I can help with?"
options.explanation: Parsing natural language to decide termination is an anti-pattern. Phrasing varies between responses, and the model can use a closing phrase before the work is done.

options.text: Keep the text check, but require at least three iterations before the loop is allowed to exit.
options.explanation: An iteration count has no relationship to task completion. Simple requests would loop needlessly, and longer ones could still be cut off at the first text block after the third iteration.

options.text: Instruct the model in the system prompt never to produce text in the same response as a tool call, so that a text block always means the turn is complete.
options.explanation: A prompt instruction is probabilistic and leaves the faulty termination logic in place. Any response that still mixes text with a tool call would end the loop early.

questions.taskStatement: 5.1 Manage conversation context to preserve critical information across long interactions
questions.stem:
In long support conversations, older turns are progressively summarised to save context. Late in one chat the agent tells a customer that "a refund of around a hundred dollars was discussed some time ago". The actual figures were $118.40, promised on 4 March, for order 77213.

What should the architect change?

options.text: Extract transactional facts (amounts, dates, order numbers) into a persistent case-facts block included in every prompt.
options.explanation: Correct. Progressive summarisation condenses precise values into vague statements. Keeping the facts in a separate, persistent block protects them.

options.text: Summarise more aggressively, so that more context is left for recent messages and the model can attend to what the customer is saying now.
options.explanation: More aggressive summarisation loses more of the precise values that are already being lost.

options.text: Add to the summarisation prompt: "Try to keep important details."
options.explanation: This is vague, and the facts would still pass through repeated rounds of lossy condensation.

options.text: Stop summarising and drop the oldest turns once the context is full.
options.explanation: Dropping the oldest turns removes the commitment about the refund entirely instead of blurring it.
